newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, soyoil falters on Census.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends mixed, soyoil falters on Census.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended mixed on Thursday with greater-than-expected USDA weekly export sales supporting old crop, traders said.
Soyoil struggled with lackluster export sales and a bearish U.S. Census Bureau report.

Support for soymeal came early from USDA's weekly export sales report which pegged U.S. net export sales of soymeal during the week ended April 17 at 74,600 tonnes, above expectations for 40,000 to 60,000 tonnes.
But soyoil sales at 5,200 tonnes were at the low end of expectations for 5,000 to 15,000 tonnes.

Census pegged soymeal stocks at 322,623 tons, above expectations for 220,000 to 300,000 tons. Soyoil stocks at 2.170 million lbs were at the high end of expectations for 1.97 million to 2.19 million lbs.

Some trade sources also cited talk an Argentine firm pegged Argentine's soybean production this year at 11.0 to 11.5 million tonnes, well below USDA's expectations for 13.25 million tonnes but above some estimates for 10 million.
Soymeal closed $1.60 per ton higher to $0.90 lower with May up $0.60 at $273.00 a ton. Soyoil ended steady to 0.08 cent per lb lower with May down 0.08 at 24.85 cents.

On the day, Cargill Inc sold 200 lots May soymeal while Produce Grain, ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp and E.D. and F. Man International each sold 100 July, pit sources said. Continental Grain bought 200 July and Refco Inc and Prudential Securities each bought 100 July.
In soyoil, Refco Inc sold 300 July and 100 December, Iowa Grain and Tenco Inc each sold 200 July and ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp sold 150 July, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 18,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 14,323 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 25,000 lots, against Wednesday's 30,527.
